## The problem in one slide

Re-encode all **monochrome** legacy AVIs (h264_nvenc gbrp + mpeg4
yuv420p) into the
[OFFLINE_8BIT file standard](https://allenneuraldynamics.github.io/aind-file-standards/file_formats/behavior_videos/).

::: {.stat-grid}
::: {.stat}
[~10,840]{.num}
[mono videos]{.cap}
:::
::: {.stat}
[~228 TB]{.num}
[source on S3]{.cap}
:::
::: {.stat}
[~19.1 B]{.num}
[frames]{.cap}
:::
::: {.stat}
[~14,400 hrs]{.num}
[of video]{.cap}
:::
:::

::: {.ask-block}
That's **97%** of the 11,194-file AVI inventory. This will do three things: 1) put files in a standard color space (BT.709) with correct metadata, 2) reduce storage by ~150 TB, and 3) make the videos directly usable for analysis and consumption without a decode/convert step.
:::

::: {.small-table}

| c7a (Zen 4)       | 46                   | ~4,440           | \$1.40       | ~\$1,630           |
| c8g (Graviton 4)  | 34                   | ~3,280           | \$1.10       | ~\$1,730           |

::: {.smaller}
Benchmarked on .2xlarge at slow / CRF 18, n=8 of 8 vCPUs.

**Zen 5 wins decisively** — wider front-end and AMD's libx264-friendly SMT
beat Granite Rapids and Graviton 4's no-SMT model.
c8g is per-core memory-bandwidth limited at full load.

Spot cost is flat in compute-hours. Fanout trades wallclock for instance
count at constant \$/batch. Add ~4% for orchestration overhead → **~\$1,350**.
:::

**Impact of compression**

- ~228 TB in → **~75 TB** out
- Storage delta: **−150 TB**

**The catch with spot instances**

- Instances can vanish at ~2-min notice.
- At this scale, that *will* happen.
- Architecture absorbs it (next slides).
:::

## The pipeline at a glance

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
flowchart LR
    INV["S3 inventory CSV"] --> PB["pre-batch checks"]
    PB --> MAN["manifest.jsonl"]
    PB --> Q[("SQS work queue")]
    Q -- "lease one msg" --> W["worker pool"]
    SRC["S3 source AVIs"] -.HTTPS.-> W
    W --> CHUNKS["S3 transcoded chunks"]
    CHUNKS --> CONCAT["Concatenation"]
    CONCAT --> FINAL["final MP4s on S3"]
```

::: {.arch-callout}
One source video → one SQS message → one worker → many chunks on S3. Concat
runs once the queue is empty and glues chunks into a final MP4
without re-encoding.
:::

## Vocabulary

::: {.small-table}
| term | definition |
|-------|------------|
| **Manifest** | JSONL list of `(source URL, output paths, expected frames)` — the ground truth for what to encode. |
| **SQS** | AWS **Simple Queue Service**. A managed distributed queue. We push one **message** per source video; workers `ReceiveMessage` to claim one, `DeleteMessage` on success. |
| **Lease** | When a worker receives a message, SQS hides it from other workers for a timeout (here: 7,200 s). If the worker doesn't delete it in time, the message becomes visible again and another worker can claim it. |
| **Worker** | One process per vCPU on a c8a node. Encodes one source video at a time. |
| **Chunk** | ~2 min of encoded output (60,000 frames) as its own MKV, uploaded to S3 mid-encode. |
| **Canonical marker** | A tiny JSON in S3 that promotes a staged chunk into "officially part of the timeline." |
| **Concat** | Final pass that glues canonical chunks into one MP4 with `-c copy` (no re-encode). |
:::

## Bounding lost work

If something kills a worker mid-encode, we want **everything already done to stay done**.

::: {.small-table .autosize-table}
| mechanism | role |
|---|---|
| **Chunks (vs one big output)** | Commit partial progress to S3 every ~20 min wallclock. Worst-case lost work = one chunk's CPU, not the whole video. |
| **Concat as a separate phase** | Workers just upload chunks. Final MP4 built later from canonical markers via `ffmpeg -c copy` — no re-encode, re-runnable. |
:::

::: {.smaller-block}
A failure event hits the whole VM (96 workers at once), not one worker. Worst-case lost work scales accordingly:<br>
**Clean preempt** (2-min notice): all 96 ffmpegs flush → uploads drain → lost work ≈ 0.<br>
**Hard VM death** (OOM, kernel panic, network partition): all 96 in-flight chunks vanish → lost work ≤ 96 chunks.
:::

## Preventing writer races {.smaller}

SQS is **at-least-once**. Under rare conditions, two workers can hold the same message and both be actively encoding:

::: {.smaller}
- Heartbeat call failed silently and the lease expired
- SQS itself delivered the message twice (documented behavior)
- Worker A is stuck but not dead; B grabs the now-visible message
:::

::: {.autosize-table}
| mechanism | role |
|---|---|
| **Canonical markers (atomic create)** | One marker wins per chunk index. `IfNoneMatch:"*"` is atomic; the loser raises a conflict and bails. |
| **Markers, not S3 listings, define the timeline** | Two workers can produce `chunk_00042.mkv` in their own staging paths without colliding. The marker is what makes one of them "official". |
:::

::: {.arch-callout}
**Multiple levels of race protection.** SQS *tries* to ensure one worker per message; canonical markers enforce one writer per chunk index regardless of what SQS does.
:::

## Keeping work flowing

::: {.small-table .autosize-table}
| mechanism | role |
|---|---|
| **SQS queue with leases** | Distributes work + retries failures. Soft "this message is mine" claim, no separate coordinator. |
| **Lease heartbeat** | `ChangeMessageVisibility` every 5 min — encodes longer than the default 2 hr lease keep their claim alive. |
| **Fail-closed on lease loss** | If we can't prove we still own the message, kill ffmpeg. Marker races are *handled*; not creating them is cheaper. |
| **DLQ (Dead-Letter Queue)** | After 4 receives, SQS sets the message aside — prevents corrupt sources from cycling forever. |
:::

## Preemption rate & cost {.smaller}

[AWS Spot Instance Advisor](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/spot/instance-advisor/) reports interrupt rates as **monthly probability per running instance**. For our chosen sizes:

- **c8a.48xlarge** — 5-10%/month
- **c8a.24xlarge** — 10-15%/month
- (we exclude c8a.16xl, c8a.12xl — both in the >20% bucket)

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**Fleet preempt math** (e.g. 4× c8a.24xl + 1× c8a.48xl × 4.5 days)

- ~24 instance-days of runtime ≈ 0.8 instance-months
- Effective ~7-12% monthly rate across the mix → **~0.05-0.10 expected preempts** over the batch
- A VM kill takes all 96-192 workers on it down at once
- Each worker loses ≤1 in-flight chunk = ~0.25 vCPU-hr
- **Worst case (all preempts drain-fail, all-192-vCPU node hit):** 0.1 × 192 × 0.25 ≈ **5 vCPU-hr** out of ~82,000 → **&lt;0.01%**
- Realistic case (clean preempt with 2-min notice → drain succeeds): **≈ 0**
:::
::: {}
**Why this matters**

- We don't need to over-build for preempts — the architecture absorbs them.
- `Type: maintain` replaces preempted instances within minutes.
- The redrive limit (DLQ at 4 attempts) catches stuck messages without bias toward retry storms.
- Spot premium vs on-demand for c8a.24xl: **~70% discount** (\$1.55 vs \$5.27/hr).
:::
:::

::: {.arch-callout}
**The expensive failure isn't preempts — it's a silent wrong-result.** That's
why the architecture spends correctness budget on canonical/staging,
contiguous markers, and fail-closed lease loss, rather than minimizing
chunk size or hedging duplicate encodes.
:::

## Inner loop — single-source encode

One ffmpeg per source video. The segment muxer splits output on natural
IDRs, no `-ss` seek, no per-chunk decode-from-zero.

```bash
ffmpeg -i s3-source.avi \
  -vf "select=gte(n,FRAME_START),setpts=N/FPS/TB,$OFFLINE_8BIT_FILTERS" \
  -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -pix_fmt yuv420p \
  -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 \
  -f segment -segment_time $(( CHUNK_FRAMES / FPS )) \
  -reset_timestamps 1 -segment_format mkv \
  -segment_start_number START_K \
  -segment_list segments.csv -segment_list_type csv \
  -threads 1 \
  chunk_%05d.mkv
```

::: {.arch-callout}
**Frame-index, not time.** `select=gte(n, FRAME_START)` drops frames before
the encoder. `setpts=N/FPS/TB` synthesizes fresh PTS so source PTS jitter
can't propagate. **No `-ss`** — input-side seek in our AVIs skips 5-7
frames past the target (verified via framemd5).
:::

## Inner loop — chunk lifecycle {.smaller .scrollable}

Sidecar tails `segments.csv` while ffmpeg runs and uploads each chunk as it
closes.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
%%| fig-height: 4.5
%%{init: {'sequence': {'actorFontSize': 12, 'noteFontSize': 11, 'messageFontSize': 11, 'boxMargin': 6, 'boxTextMargin': 4, 'noteMargin': 6, 'messageMargin': 28}}}%%
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant FF as ffmpeg (segment muxer)
    participant SC as sidecar thread
    participant S3 as S3
    FF->>SC: segments.csv row appended (chunk_00042.mkv)
    SC->>SC: rename → chunk_00042_n60123.mkv
    SC->>S3: PUT staging/.../chunk_00042_n60123.mkv
    S3-->>SC: 200 OK
    SC->>S3: PUT canonical/chunk_00042.json (IfNoneMatch:"*")
    alt first writer wins
        S3-->>SC: 200 OK — promoted
    else losing worker
        S3-->>SC: 412 PreconditionFailed
        SC->>SC: raise CanonicalPromotionConflict
    end
```

::: {.arch-callout}
**Staging is attempt-scoped, canonical is global.** A late upload from a
losing worker can't enter the timeline. Resume + concat read only canonical
markers; staging is opaque to them.
:::

## Inner loop — resume {.smaller}

Worker boot: LIST `canonical/`, derive resume state from markers only.

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**Marker JSON**

```json
{
  "k": 42,
  "n_frames": 60123,
  "staged_key": "staging/.../chunk_00042_n60123.mkv",
  "attempt_id": "i-0abc.../1718...",
  "uploaded_at": "2026-06-17T..."
}
```
:::
::: {}
**Gap-free by construction**

Canonical markers are always a contiguous run `0..K-1`. The sidecar's `_promote_ready` only writes marker `N+1` after marker `N` is in place — never skips. If resume ever sees a gap, it **refuses** rather than guessing what should fill it.

**Resume state from markers:**

- `K = max(k) + 1`
- `frame_start = Σ n_frames`
- next ffmpeg picks up with `select=gte(n, frame_start)`
:::
:::

::: {.arch-callout}
`IfNoneMatch:"*"` handles a **separate** concern from contiguity above. Contiguity (no gaps) comes from the sidecar's strictly sequential promotion. Coherence (one writer per slot) is what the atomic claim adds: the loser's PUT returns 412, its sidecar bails immediately, and SQS redrives the message. Without the atomic guarantee, both PUTs would silently succeed (last-write-wins), the loser would keep racing on every subsequent slot, and the marker's `staged_key` would flip unpredictably between attempts.
:::

## Sizing the chunks {.smaller}

`CHUNK_FRAMES_NOMINAL = 60,000` ≡ **120 s of source @ 500 fps**

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**What changes with chunk size**

| chunk    | wallclock (encode + upload) | PUTs / worker / hr | lost work / preempt |
|----------|----------------------------:|-------------------:|--------------------:|
| 6 k (12 s) | ~2 min                     | ~30                | ≤2 min              |
| 30 k (60 s)| ~9 min                     | ~7                 | ≤9 min              |
| **60 k (120 s)** | **~20 min**          | **~3**             | **≤20 min**         |
| 300 k (10 min) | ~80 min                | ~0.7               | ≤80 min             |
:::
::: {}
**Why 60,000**

- libx264 default `keyint=250` produces IDRs every 0.5 s; the segment muxer cuts at the **next IDR** after each `segment_time` boundary → real chunks vary by ≤0.5 s, well under nominal.
- ~3 S3 PUTs / worker / hr × 96 workers = ~290 PUTs/hr — well below S3's 3,500-write/s prefix limit.
- Lost-work expectation per preempt fits inside one spot-warning window (~120 s).
- Marker overhead (one ~400 B JSON per chunk) amortizes nicely across ~30,000 total markers.

**No `force_key_frames`** — relying on the natural IDR cadence saves ~0.5% bitrate vs. rigid segment boundaries.
:::
:::

## Where the bytes flow {.smaller}

Source AVIs are streamed straight from S3 to ffmpeg — **no local staging**.

::: {.small-table}
| layer                                | throughput / cost                          | role this batch |
|--------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| **S3 GET, intra-region**             | ~10 GB/s per bucket, **\$0 egress**         | source AVIs (one stream per worker) |
| c8a.24xl network (sustained)         | ~12.5 Gbps                                 | covers ~250× worker bandwidth |
| **EBS gp3 root (default)**           | 125 MB/s base, 250 MB/s burst              | OS + ffmpeg binary only |
| **Instance-store NVMe**              | not provisioned on c8a (CPU-optimized)     | n/a |
| S3 PUT (chunks + markers)            | ~3,500 writes/s/prefix                     | upload path; per-worker bound |
:::

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**Source-side budget**

- Per file: ~47 Mbps ≈ **5.9 MB/s**
- 96 workers/instance × 5.9 = ~**565 MB/s = 4.5 Gbps**
- Well under the 12.5 Gbps sustained network ceiling.
- `-reconnect 1 -reconnect_streamed 1 -reconnect_delay_max 30` covers transient TCP blips without re-decoding from frame 0.
:::
::: {}
**Why we don't stage to EBS**

- gp3 baseline 125 MB/s → ~4× **slower** than aggregate S3 GET to RAM.
- Extra round-trip (S3 → EBS → ffmpeg) + ~\$0.08/GB-mo storage.
- Intra-region S3 GET is free in dollars and nearly free in latency.
- HTTPS-direct was validated in `test_s3_direct.py`: bit-identical output, no measurable throughput penalty.
:::
:::

## Worker loop {.scrollable}

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
flowchart TD
    R["ReceiveMessage"] --> RS["get_resume_state"]
    RS -- "already complete" --> ACK_EARLY["DeleteMessage → loop"]
    RS -- "work remains" --> RUN["build_encode_cmd → spawn ffmpeg"]
    RUN --> HB["ChangeMessageVisibility(2hr)<br>& lease heartbeat (300s)"]
    RUN --> SC["Sidecar thread:<br>stage + canonical PUT"]
    RUN --> SIG["SIGUSR1 handler:<br>set preempt flag, SIGTERM ffmpeg"]
    HB --> EXIT["ffmpeg exits"]
    SC --> EXIT
    SIG --> EXIT
    EXIT --> DRAIN["sidecar drain (≤ 600s):<br>promote final chunks"]
    DRAIN -- "success" --> OK["DeleteMessage"]
    DRAIN -- "preempted" --> PRE["SetVisibility(0)"]
    DRAIN -- "failed" --> FAIL["raise → release lease"]
```

## Worker — concurrency safety {.smaller}

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**`_WorkerState` with `RLock`**

- `current_receipt` (mutated across receive/delete)
- `ffmpeg_proc` (mutated by main, read by SIGUSR1 & heartbeat)
- `preempting` flag

All transitions through helpers:
`set_receipt`, `clear_receipt`,
`set_ffmpeg_proc`, `request_ffmpeg_terminate`,
`snapshot_for_extension`.
:::
::: {}
**Races that we close**

- `Popen` → `set_ffmpeg_proc` window: re-check `preempting` under lock after registration.
- Heartbeat reading half-cleared receipt: snapshot under lock.
- Already-complete ack: snapshot receipt **before** delete, clear **after** success.
- Lease-extender failure: ffmpeg SIGTERM, fail attempt, **don't** keep writing.
:::
:::

::: {.arch-callout}
**Fail-closed on lease loss.** If we can't prove we still own the message,
we stop writing. Better to redo one video than risk two workers racing on
canonical promotion.
:::

## SQS orchestration — pre-batch

CSV inventory → one SQS message per (`video_id`, `camera`).

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
flowchart LR
    CSV["avi_real.csv (asset_id, camera, s3_url, ...)"] --> FILT["filter: codec / pix_fmt / width"]
    FILT --> CC["collision check:<br>source_s3, output_chunks_prefix,<br>output_final_s3"]
    CC --> M["manifest.jsonl (uploaded for audit)"]
    CC --> SQS["SendMessageBatch ×10 → SQS work queue"]
    CC --> EV["status/events/...queued.jsonl"]
```

## SQS orchestration — message shape

```json
{
  "video_id": "asset-1",
  "camera": "side",
  "source_https": "https://aind-open-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/.../side.avi",
  "source_s3":    "s3://aind-open-data/.../side.avi",
  "output_chunks_prefix": "s3://aind-encoded-data/encoded/v1/chunks/aind-open-data/.../side/",
  "output_final_s3":      "s3://aind-encoded-data/encoded/v1/final/aind-open-data/.../side.mp4",
  "fps": 500.0,
  "expected_frames": 2520000,
  "chunk_frames": 60000
}
```

::: {.arch-callout}
**Output paths are manifest-owned, not derived.** Source-mirrored layout
(`urllib.parse.quote()` on the source S3 key) so the audit trail
round-trips back to the source bucket — no `video_id`/camera collisions
across projects.
:::

```{mermaid}
    DLQ["DLQ (maxReceiveCount=4)"]
    QM -- "ReceiveMessage" --> W
    W -- "DeleteMessage (success)" --> QM
    W -- "ChangeMessageVisibility(7200) every 300s" --> QM
    W -- "ChangeMessageVisibility(0) on preempt drain" --> QM
    QM -- "after 4 receives" --> DLQ
```

::: {.arch-callout}
- **One message = one source video**, not one chunk. Encode is cheap to
  resume; chunking the SQS layer would multiply duplicate-claim risk.
- **DLQ at 4 attempts** catches persistent failures (corrupt source,
  unreachable URL) without flooding the queue.
:::

## Spot fleet orchestration {.smaller}

```jsonc
{
  "Type": "maintain",               // auto-replace preempted instances
  "TargetCapacity": 384,            // vCPU
  "TargetCapacityUnitType": "vcpu",
  "AllocationStrategy": "capacityOptimized",
  "InstanceInterruptionBehavior": "terminate",

  "LaunchTemplateConfigs": [{
    "LaunchTemplateSpecification": {
      "LaunchTemplateName": "aind-transcode-c8a",
      "Version": "$Latest"
    },
    "Overrides": [
      { "InstanceType": "c8a.48xlarge" },   // 5-10% monthly preempt
      { "InstanceType": "c8a.24xlarge" }    // 10-15% monthly preempt
    ]
  }]
}
```

::: {.arch-callout}
- **`capacityOptimized`** — AWS picks the deepest spot pool at each launch
  → fewer interruptions than `lowestPrice`.
- **Only the two best preempt-rate sizes.** c8a.16xl and c8a.12xl are both in the >20% bucket; we skip them. Bare-metal sizes also excluded (slower boot, no throughput benefit).
- **vCPU as the unit** — fleet hits 384 vCPU via 2× 48xl, 4× 24xl, or a mix, whichever AWS has deepest at launch.
- **`maintain`** — preempted nodes are replaced automatically until the queue drains.
:::

## EC2 instance lifecycle

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
flowchart TD
    L["EC2 spot launch"] --> U["user-data.sh: install ffmpeg + Python,<br>pip install, spawn workers per vCPU,<br>start watcher"]
    U --> WATCH["IMDSv2 watcher polls /spot/instance-action"]
    WATCH -- "interruption notice" --> KILL["kill -USR1 every worker pid"]
    KILL --> DRAIN["workers drain and release SQS"]
    DRAIN --> TERM["EC2 terminates ~120s later"]
    U --> WLOOP["each worker:<br>receive → encode → drain → delete,<br>exit on 2 empty polls"]
```

## Concat phase {.smaller}

```bash
uv run backlog-concat                        # iterates manifest rows; idempotent
uv run backlog-concat --delete-staging-after-concat   # opt-in cleanup
```

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**Per manifest row**

1. LIST `canonical/`
2. assert contiguous markers
3. download staged MKVs
4. `ffmpeg -f concat -c copy` → MP4
5. write `*.processing.json` ([aind-data-schema](https://github.com/AllenNeuralDynamics/aind-data-schema) `DataProcess`)
6. write per-video audit JSON
7. PUT final MP4 to `output_final_s3`
:::
::: {}
**MP4 metadata = persistent provenance**

- `source_s3`, `transcoder`, `encoder`
- `profile`, `transcoded_at`, `author`

**Audit JSON = operational state**

- `chunk_count`, `canonical_marker_count`
- staging object count + bytes
- staging delete results
- chunk-level checksums + lineage
:::
:::

## Observability — status table

Best-effort JSONL events at:

```text
s3://$OUTPUT_BUCKET/$PREFIX/status/events/batch_id=<id>/event_date=<date>/*.jsonl
```

::: {.small-table}
| phase / status                          | written by   |
|-----------------------------------------|--------------|
| `pre_batch/queued`                      | pre-batch    |
| `worker/encode_started`                 | worker       |
| `worker/encode_completed`               | worker       |
| `worker/already_complete`               | worker       |
| `worker/preempted`                      | worker       |
| `worker/failed`                         | worker       |
| `concat/{completed,skipped_*,failed}`   | concat       |
:::

::: {.arch-callout}
**Reporting only.** SQS owns work leasing; canonical markers own resume
truth. The status table is Athena-queryable for "how is the batch doing
right now?" without touching the control plane.
:::

## Verification + failure handling {.smaller}

::: {.two-col}
::: {}
**Verification (fail-closed)**

- Pre-concat: contiguous canonical markers
- Post-concat: MP4 frame count == `Σ n_frames`
- Pipeline-level: `scripts/verify.sh` walks the manifest, reports drift
- Any mismatch is a **batch failure**, never a warning
:::
::: {}
**Failure modes**

- **Spot preempt:** SIGUSR1 → drain → vis(0)
- **Network blip:** `-reconnect` + sidecar retry
- **Lease loss:** SIGTERM ffmpeg, fail attempt
- **Marker collision:** `IfNoneMatch:"*"` — losing worker raises
- **Persistent failure:** DLQ at attempt 4
- **Concat collision:** idempotent on `(final, audit)` pair
:::
:::

- **Production launch:** small-pilot first (`LIMIT=50`), validate, then full.
- **Audit ID disambiguation in DataProcess key** — `(video_id, camera)`
  alone collides if two source URLs share that pair; will add audit_id.
- **S3 chaos tests** — interrupted PUT, marker conflict mid-stage.
- **Lifecycle policy** — auto-expire orphan staging objects from killed
  attempts (canonical never expires).

## Summary {.smaller}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="47%"}
**Encoder & instance choice**

- `slow / CRF 18` is the visible quality knee
- `c8a.24xlarge` spot wins on throughput and \$/throughput
- Whole batch: ~\$1,350 @ 8× c8a.24xl in ~4.5 days
:::
::: {.column width="47%"}
**Architecture**

- One ffmpeg per source, segment muxer, frame-index resume
- Canonical/staging split — atomic marker promotion
- SQS heartbeat + fail-closed on lease loss
- Spot fleet `maintain` + `capacityOptimized`
- Idempotent concat, manifest-driven verify
:::
:::
